Nations Championship - England 37-12 New Zealand: Most complete performance under Steve Borthwick sees hosts stay in title hunt
Henry Slade, Jack van Poortvliet, Ben Earl, Ollie Chessum, Seb Atkinson score tries as England totally outplay New Zealand in Saturday's Nations Championship at Allianz Stadium Twickenham; Steve Borthwick's side will make final unless France beat Argentina with a bonus point in Paris
By Michael Cantillon at Allianz Stadium Twickenham
Last Updated: 21/11/26 4:05pm
A performance full of pace, power and verve saw England outplay New Zealand at home for the second year in a row, beating the All Blacks 37-12 in Saturday's Nations Championship, giving themselves a chance of winning the title.
Last year, England picked up their first win over New Zealand for 13 years at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, but this success at the same venue was even more impressive, and leaves France needing to beat Argentina with a bonus point to stop England making the final.
Outside-centre Henry Slade, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet, No 8 Ben Earl, blindside flanker Ollie Chessum and inside-centre Seb Atkinson scored tries as England totally dominated.
England 37-12 New Zealand - Score summary
England - Tries: Slade (5), van Poortvliet (32), Earl (36), Chessum (43), Atkinson (63). Cons: F Smith (32, 37), M Smith (64). Pens: M Smith (57, 80+1).
New Zealand - Tries: De Groot (39), B Barrett (52). Cons: McKenzie (52).
A week on from their shock defeat to Wales in Cardiff - a first against the Welsh since 1953 - New Zealand scored two tries through prop Ethan de Groot and full-back Beauden Barrett, but the visitors were hugely disappointing in attack and at the set-piece, while they also shipped far too many penalties.
Former England World Cup winner Lewis Moody, living with motor neurone disease, emerged to stand with England's squad as they faced the haka in a unique and moving moment pre-kick-off. The home side never looked back from there.
What's next?
Next week sees the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend, to be staged at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, over Friday November 27, Saturday 28 and Sunday 29.
Wherever each northern hemisphere nation finishes in their table decides who they will face next weekend, setting up Tests with the corresponding finishers in the southern hemisphere.
Despite victory vs the All Blacks, England are likely to finish second in their group, with France expected to beat Argentina well later on Saturday.
England's Nations Championship fixtures and results
Should that happen, Steve Borthwick's men will face either a rematch with New Zealand or play South Africa on Saturday November 28 (4.40pm), depending on how the Springboks get on in Dublin later.
For New Zealand, they must now wait to see how South Africa get on in Dublin. If they finish second, they will likely face England on Saturday November 28 (4.40pm), while if they finish top, they would face France in the Nations Championship final next Sunday November 29 (4.40pm), should Les Bleus defeat Argentina later.
